title: Digital transformation and consumer financial behavior: a quantitative systematic review of digital financial literacy as a dynamic capability
summary: Abstract This study examines how digital transformation is associated with digital financial literacy (DFL) and consumer financial behavior within technology-enabled financial ecosystems. The study synthesizes evidence from the literature and develops an explanatory framework in which DFL is conceptualized as a dynamic capability that functions as an intervening mechanism linking digital exposure, financial learning, and behavioral outcomes. A quantitative systematic literature review was conducted using Scopus and Web of Science, covering studies published between 2014 and 2025. The final corpus comprised 98 peer-reviewed journal articles aligned with the research question, including empirical, quantitative, and review-based studies. The analysis combined bibliometric mapping, author co-citation analysis, article-level coded evidence, Jaccard coefficients, Fisher’s exact tests, chi-square tests, and hierarchical decision-tree modeling. The re-estimated article-level evidence indicates that digital transformation and digital financial literacy frequently co-occur in the reviewed literature (Jaccard = 0.771). However, this broad association is not statistically significant according to Fisher’s exact test. The strongest evidence emerges from the targeted transformation-to-literacy coding, which is strongly associated with the presence of financial literacy (Jaccard = 0.909; Fisher p < 0.001; chi-square p < 0.001). By contrast, associations involving financial behavior are weaker and statistically unsupported. Decision-tree analysis further identifies technology use, income, and education as salient capability conditions, indicating that digital financial capability continues to be shaped by socioeconomic resources. The study contributes by conceptualizing DFL as a dynamic capability that evolves through technological engagement, behavioral learning, institutional trust, and governance conditions. Methodologically, it demonstrates a transparent and reproducible approach for integrating bibliometric mapping with inferential evidence synthesis in systematic literature reviews while explicitly acknowledging the limitations of article-level coded evidence, open-access sampling, and non-causal inference. The findings are consistent with the interpretation that digital transformation is associated with DFL as an evolving dynamic capability. However, the weaker, non-significant associations with financial behavior indicate that this capability-based reading should be treated as a plausible explanatory framework rather than a confirmed causal pathway.

title: Trends in zakat research across Indonesia–Malaysia: governance, trust and digitalization
summary: Purpose This study aims to map the landscape of zakat research in Indonesia and Malaysia along three principal axes: (i) governance and accountability, (ii) literacy, trust and compliance and (iii) digitalization/fintech – and synthesizes the policy implications for strengthening the zakat ecosystem. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative bibliometric design was used using Scopus and Web of Science metadata. Performance analysis and science mapping were conducted with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer, while PRISMA guided study screening. Visual outputs include three-field plots, word clouds, treemaps, dynamic trends, trend topics, co-occurrence and author-density networks and a thematic map. Findings Publications surge after 2017 and peak in 2024, signalling a growing critical mass of authors, outlets and citation networks. Keyword mapping positions zakat as a hub connecting (a) development themes (poverty, Sustainable Development Goals and inclusion), (b) governance themes (accountability, corporate governance and performance) and (c) digital innovation (fintech, blockchain and technology acceptance model/unified theory of acceptance and use of technology). Religiosity and trust act as bridges from governance and literacy to compliance and the adoption of digital channels. Thematic mapping classifies sustainability and finance/fintech with blockchain as motor themes, while zakat, Indonesia and Malaysia emerge as basic themes highly central but requiring deeper operationalization. Practical implications The synthesis yields three policy recommendations: (1) standardize accountability indicators and digital-service performance metrics for zakat institutions; (2) design context-specific digital strategies across countries that account for social influence and infrastructure; and (3) strengthen empirical models that integrate institutional variation, behavioral factors and technology to improve compliance and outreach. Originality/value The paper contributes an integrated framework that bridges normative debates with bibliometric evidence, offering a coherent path to enhance compliance, public trust and the development impact of the zakat ecosystem in Indonesia and Malaysia.

title: Qualitative Inquiry into FinTech Operation in Nigeria: A User Perspective
summary: This study examines FinTech operations in Nigeria through the lens of user experiences with mobile payment platforms. Adopting a qualitative research design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with twenty six informants, comprising salaried employees, self-employed individuals, and tertiary education students. The analysis revealed three key themes: poor internet connectivity, cashless policy and fraud concerns. Findings indicate that while FinTech presents significant opportunities for enhancing financial inclusion and improving service delivery, user perceptions are shaped by a complex interplay of institutional forces. Specifically, the regulative pillar influences security, compliance, and legitimacy; the normative pillar affects social acceptance and cultural alignment; while the cognitive pillar shapes users’ understanding of risks and benefits. The study further reveals that persistent challenges such as fraud, inadequate infrastructure, and regulatory gaps undermine user trust in FinTech platforms, thus, signifying digital risk. Consequently, strengthening internet infrastructure, enhancing cybersecurity measures, and improving regulatory frameworks are critical to ensuring sustainable growth in the sector. In conclusion, reliable and high-speed internet connectivity is essential for reducing transaction failures, while issues such as financial risk, legal uncertainty, and privacy concerns remain significant barriers to adoption. The study contributes to existing literature by offering qualitative insights into user experiences and demonstrating how institutional forces influence FinTech adoption and trust in Nigeria.

title: Kontorovich–Lebedev Calculus for Digital-Twin Telemetry, Battery Packs, and Quantum-Ready Logistics
summary: Within an operator-theoretic framework for spectral analysis, the KL transform is formulated as a calculus for traces generated by sustainable logistics, electric-vehicle battery systems, intelligent transportation telemetry, and digital-twin supply networks. The kernel is the modified Bessel function of imaginary order, represented through a Fourier integral that remains real and even with respect to the spectral index. Analytic continuation into a vertical strip provides a uniform majorant capable of accommodating quantization effects, contact-resistance spikes, and demand shocks. Asymptotic behavior at both the origin and infinity determines the natural domain as a scale of weighted Lebesgue spaces encompassing the standard and weighted classes required for current, voltage, irradiance, and order-flow signals. An adjoint identity transforms forward KL analysis into a reconstruction formula appropriate for extracting residues associated with multi-scale logistics modes and for preconditioning combinatorial assignments that subsequently enter a quantum-annealing layer. The treatment remains theoretical and operator-theoretic, with numerical illustrations restricted to schematic envelopes rather than empirical field trials. Keywords: Kontorovich–Lebedev transform; modified Bessel kernel; adjoint operator; uniform estimates; spectral residues; battery telemetry; smart mobility; supply-chain resilience; digital twins; quantum logistics.

title: Influence of ESG Compliance on Product Safety Performance : Evidence from Indian Manufacturing Firms
summary: The study examines the impact of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) compliance on Product safety Performance in Indian manufacturing firms, a relationship that remains underexplored in emerging marktets. The research aims to assess how individual ESG components- Environmental Compliance (EC), Social Responsibility, (SR), and Governance Practices (GP) - influence product safety outcomes and how overall ESG integration contributes to safer manufacturing operations. Primary data were collected through a structured quetionnaire, and a sample of Indian manufacturing firms was analyzed using Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), correlation analysis and Structural Equation Modelling( SEM). the results confirm strong reliability and validity of the measurement model and reveal significant positive effects of all ESG dimensions on product safety, with Governance Practices emerging as the strongest predictor. the composite ESG construct also demonstrates a substantial positive influence on product safety outcomes. The study offers practical implications for policymakers, industry leaders, and investors by emphasizing ESG integration as a strategic tool for improving product safety and operational excellence. This research contributes novel empirical evidence linking ESG compliance and product safety performance in the Indian manufacturing sector.

title: Village Officials' Human Flourishing: Phenomenology of Public Service Digital Transformation, Ipir, Sikka
summary: Centralized digital migration policies trigger exogenous shocks, creating severe normative asymmetry and institutional fragmentation within rural bureaucracies. This research aimed to dismantle the lived experiences of village officials negotiating this systemic crisis by employing a transcendental phenomenological approach in Ipir Village. Through comprehensive interviews and participant observation, empirical findings confirmed that infrastructure disparities ironically compelled frontline bureaucrats to mobilize empathetic discretion to mitigate mechanical system paralysis. Furthermore, severe cognitive pressure was effectively mitigated through intergenerational collaborative governance and a distributed accountability ecosystem. This adaptation process organically catalyzes psychological resilience, transforming technological stuttering into profound environmental mastery and existential meaningfulness in public service delivery. Departing from conventional technocentric reductionism, this study affirms that state bureaucratic resilience is fundamentally sustained by the reliability of human infrastructure. As a prescriptive implication, national policymakers must adopt humanistic institutional design engineering that strictly institutionalizes robust protection systems for the psychological welfare of every state apparatus.

title: Digital Transformation and Governance in Indonesian Islamic Boarding Schools: A Comparative Study of Two Pesantren
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping how Islamic boarding schools (pesantren) organize administration, learning, communication, and stakeholder services. This study primarily employed a qualitative approach within a convergent mixed-method design to examine how two pesantren respond to digital change, identify its effects on institutional governance, and formulate a value-based model for digital transformation. Qualitative data were obtained through interviews, participatory observations, and document analysis, while quantitative data from a structured questionnaire administered to 30 students were used to support and triangulate the qualitative findings. The analysis revealed an adaptive-selective strategy: technology is adopted when it aligns with institutional values, provides practical benefits, and presents manageable risks. Digitalization improves administrative efficiency, access to learning resources, communication with parents, transparency, and public trust, while face-to-face Qur'anic transmission, bandongan, sorogan, and character formation remain central. Key challenges include unequal digital literacy, infrastructure and maintenance costs, data-security risks, inappropriate content, and fragmented systems. Based on these two institutional cases, the study proposes an Adaptive-Conservative Model for Digital Transformation in Pesantren, consisting of value foundations, governance transformation, learning innovation, and ecosystem strengthening. The model is context-specific and requires broader empirical testing before wider application.

title: Green innovation, green investment, environmental taxation and economic development as determinants of environmental quality in OECD countries
summary: Green growth as a concept gained prominence since the beginning of the millennium, and ever since, there has been increased focus on the credibility of instruments such as green investment, green innovation, and environmental taxation as means for making sustainability compatible with economic development. Against this backdrop, the present study investigated the impact of green innovation, green investment, and environmental taxation on the environmental quality of twenty-four OECD countries from 2001 to 2023. To diagnose this macro-panel data, the study uses cross-sectional dependence diagnostics followed by second-generation panel unit root tests. CS-ARDL technique, FMOLS and DOLS methods, and Panel Quantile Regression are used to derive robust empirical insights. The findings showed that green investment and environmental taxation contribute significantly to reducing carbon emissions. It is also observed that the highest emitting countries exhibit the strongest emission abating impact of green investment and environmental taxation. However, green innovations appear to have a positive impact on carbon emissions, indicating the need for a comprehensive assessment of the rebound effect as well as the invention-diffusion gap. The study recommends the use of policy mixes for effective implementation, especially diversifying the green investments while emphasising the maximum internalization of externalities via taxation.

title: Strategic governance through ethics-by-design: aligning UI/UX practices with ESG accountability
summary: Purpose This paper aims to conceptualize ethics-by-design as a governance mechanism that positions user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) design as a critical yet underexplored layer in operationalizing environmental, social and governance (ESG) accountability. It addresses ethical and regulatory risks arising from manipulative, opaque and exclusionary interface practices and proposes integrating interface ethics into ESG disclosure and digital sustainability frameworks. Design/methodology/approach A structured conceptual synthesis is adopted, drawing on interdisciplinary literature from design ethics, ESG governance, human–computer interaction and responsible innovation. The paper develops the ethics-by-design for ESG (EbD4ESG) framework through thematic integration and analytical abstraction, supported by illustrative cross-sector examples. Findings UI/UX design decisions significantly influence user trust, informed consent and inclusion, functioning as microlevel governance mechanisms within ESG systems. These interactions, often overlooked in ESG reporting, carry regulatory, reputational and social risks. The framework highlights design as a critical link between corporate strategy and digital responsibility. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual study, the framework lacks empirical validation. Future research should focus on testing, implementation and metric standardization. Practical implications The paper offers actionable strategies for auditing, disclosing and governing ethical design within ESG structures. Social implications Interface design shapes user autonomy, inclusion and well-being, making it central to digital equity. Originality/value The paper advances a novel perspective by positioning UI/UX design as a governance interface within ESG implementation, bridging the gap between high-level ethical commitments and everyday digital interactions. It offers an original, theory-informed framework and actionable tools for integrating ethical design into ESG accountability and disclosure practices.

title: Digitalization pathways for food loss and waste prevention in agri-food supply chains: Current evidence, challenges and future directions
summary: Background Food loss and waste (FLW) remains a major challenge for global agri-food systems, generating substantial environmental, economic, and social impacts. Digitalization has emerged as a promising strategy to improve resource efficiency and support FLW prevention, yet the effectiveness of different digital technologies remains uneven and often insufficiently evaluated. Scope and approach This critical review examines the contribution of Industry 4.0 and Agriculture 4.0 technologies, including the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, blockchain, and consumer-oriented digital platforms, to FLW prevention across the entire agri-food supply chain. Rather than cataloguing technological applications, the review critically distinguishes between demonstrated reductions in FLW and improvements in technical performance that are frequently assumed to translate into waste prevention, while evaluating technological maturity, implementation barriers, and future research priorities. Key findings and conclusions IoT-enabled monitoring and smart logistics provide the strongest direct evidence for reducing spoilage risks; among AI applications, inventory management is comparatively well supported, although much of the broader AI/ML evidence remains based on operational proxies. Evidence for blockchain applications, dynamic pricing, and consumer-facing technologies remains limited or highly context dependent. Persistent barriers include fragmented data infrastructures, interoperability constraints, unequal digital capabilities, uncertain economic returns, and rebound effects. Digital technologies can contribute meaningfully to FLW prevention only when integrated with organizational, behavioural, and governance strategies. Future research should prioritize standardized impact metrics, longitudinal system-level evaluations, and integrated environmental assessments capable of quantifying real reductions in FLW and associated sustainability trade-offs.

title: Spatial frictions and asymmetric trade potential of agri-food supply chains: evidence from the Sino-Kazakh corridor
summary: Macro-level trade statistics often mask structural frictions that suppress the performance of the Sino-Kazakh agri-food supply chain. This study examines the spatial and institutional barriers systematically limiting the value of Kazakh agricultural exports to China. Drawing on Transaction Cost Economics (TCE) and a sequencing-based "master switch" perspective, we construct a multi-dimensional descriptive framework that triangulates UN Comtrade data (2013–2024) against 158 active WTO I-TIP Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) and Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) records, supplemented by CAREC Corridor Performance Measurement and Monitoring logistics data. Our analysis identifies a severe weight-value paradox: in 2024, Chinese agri-food imports from Kazakhstan were 25.8 times heavier but only 3.2 times more valuable than Chinese exports to Kazakhstan. Furthermore, under the modelled scenario, SPS protocols combined with a five-day border delay and a representative 1.2% daily quality-degradation parameter generate cumulative quality loss, creating an estimated 14.25% trade suppression rate that disproportionately targets high-value perishable commodities. A comparative analysis with the China-ASEAN and China-Europe Railway Express corridors confirms that the friction is neither geographic nor infrastructural, but entirely institutional in origin. We conclude that the dominant barrier is the absence of a bilateral SPS mutual recognition framework. To address this, we recommend two targeted policy interventions: the establishment of a comprehensive Sino-Kazakh SPS mutual recognition agreement and the deployment of a consortium blockchain-based digital customs platform. These measures would transform the Khorgos border from a physical chokepoint into a seamless digital corridor, unlocking substantial latent trade potential. title: Environmental Accounting Information Disclosure andFinancial Performance: An Empirical Analysis
summary: Purpose: This study tries to determine whether the financial performance of Bangladeshi-listed banks on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) is significantly associated with the environmental accounting information disclosure (ENVI). Design/methodology/approach: This study uses panel data from the annual reports of 34 from 36 domestic commercial banks listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) in Bangladesh, comprising 238 observations for the period 2018–2024. The non-probability sampling method (convenience procedure) was used. A robust dynamic panel estimation approach is employed, using two-step system GMM with clustered standard errors for ROA and ROE to address dynamic endogeneity and within-firm correlation, and RegHDFE with firm and year fixed effects for EPS. Findings: The study establishes that Bangladeshi banks’ ENVI has a differential consequence on financial related performance. Under robust estimation, ENVI does not exhibit a statistically significant effect on ROA, ROE, or EPS. The consistently positive direction of ENVI coefficients, however, suggests a initial relationship that may strengthen as disclosure practices mature. Originality/value: These findings provide that increasing environmental accountability by raising awareness and offering tax advantages can encourage businesses to adopt more sustainable practices. Future research should consider broader samples, longer observation periods, social governance, and other variables to better understand the enduring effects of financial performance on banking stability in emerging economies like Bangladesh.

title: Qurbani Utilisation Index (QUI-Awqaf NZ): measuring zero Qurbani waste — a methodology note for the Qurbani supply chain
summary: Awqaf New Zealand's founding claim is that the annual Qurbani (Udhiyah) is among the largest single sources of wasted charitable resource. That claim has never been measured: there is no global Qurbani census, and nowhere any count of what becomes of the animal. National and institutional counts exist in a small number of places, but they count different things by different methods, cannot be added together, and none of them measures utilisation. This methodology note proposes the Qurbani Utilisation Index (QUI-Awqaf NZ), adapting the published food-loss methodology of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) that underlies SDG indicator 12.3.1(a) to the Qurbani supply chain. The index reports the share of each animal's total value captured for social development, stage by stage as well as in total. The note contains no findings and no primary data: no farm is in operation and no capital has been deployed. It states the strongest objections to itself in full, including that Awqaf New Zealand has an interest in the answer, and is offered to universities and government research centres to carry out independently. FAO is cited solely as the source of a published methodology; it has no involvement in this work and has not reviewed it. Published in English and Arabic. Version 2 corrects a claim made in version 1, which stated that there is no national Qurbani census. The global half of that was true; the national half was not. The claim has been narrowed rather than withdrawn. The error was identified by Awqaf New Zealand against itself and is recorded, with its reasoning, as entry 006 in the organisation's public feedback log. Version 1 remains available and has not been withdrawn.

title: Do green innovation and advertising intensity enhance financial performance? Firm-level evidence from the global chemical sector
summary: The transition toward a low-carbon economy has intensified scrutiny on the environmental strategies of carbon-intensive sectors, such as the chemical industry. This paper examines the impact of green innovation on corporate financial performance (CFP), as empirical testing of the NRBV remains limited in such sectors, as well as the moderating role of advertising intensity in this relationship. In this study, advertising intensity refers to a firm's overall advertising expenditure relative to sales, which may include environmental and sustainability-related communication activities used to enhance stakeholder awareness, corporate legitimacy, and the market visibility of green initiatives. Using an unbalanced panel of 105 publicly listed chemical companies from 2015 to 2023, this study examines two dimensions of green innovation, namely, environmental performance-based innovation (EnvPS) and invention-based innovation (IS), and analyses their effects on return on equity (ROE), return on assets (ROA), and return on sales (ROS). The results of the panel regression indicate that the effect of green innovation on CFP is not significant in the short term, indicating a lack of market awareness of sustainability activities and slow returns on innovation. However, advertising intensity introduces a dual interacting role: it amplifies the financial gains associated with EnvPS, while concurrently weakening the profitability effects of IS due to increased short-term cost burdens. This study offers novel empirical evidence on how advertising intensity differentially conditions the relationship between innovation and performance in the global chemical industry, demonstrating that visibility, rather than innovation alone, is critical for converting sustainability investments into financial value.

summary: Introduction. Digital transformation is one of the key drivers of enhancing enterprise competitiveness in the digital economy. It encompasses changes in business processes, management systems, and decision-making mechanisms based on modern digital technologies. Digitalization is particularly significant in financial resource management, as it improves the efficiency of financial planning, analysis, control, and forecasting. At the same time, its implementation is accompanied by challenges related to cybersecurity, data protection, the development of employees’ digital competencies, and the modernization of digital infrastructure. Purpose. To investigate the essence of digital transformation and assess its impact on enterprise financial resource management by identifying the main benefits, risks, and prospects of applying digital technologies. Methods. The study employed the methods of analysis, synthesis, systems analysis, comparison, generalization, logical modeling, and statistical analysis. The research was based on scientific publications, analytical reports of international organizations, statistical data, and the practical experience of enterprises undergoing digital transformation. Results. The findings indicate that the implementation of digital technologies contributes to the automation of financial processes, improves the speed of information processing, enhances forecasting accuracy, strengthens the quality of managerial decision-making, and increases the effectiveness of financial flow control. The application of artificial intelligence, Big Data, cloud services, and digital platforms enables cost optimization, reduces financial risks, and improves the financial resilience of enterprises. At the same time, the study identifies the main barriers to digital transformation, including high implementation costs, insufficient digital competencies of personnel, and cybersecurity risks. Conclusions. Digital transformation is an important tool for improving the efficiency of financial resource management and strengthening enterprise competitiveness. Its effectiveness depends on the level of digital maturity, the availability of an appropriate technological infrastructure, and the implementation of a comprehensive digital risk management strategy.

title: Developing an Interpretive Structural Model of Agile Human Resources Using a Soft Capabilities Approach to Digital Transformation
summary: The present study aimed to develop an interpretive structural model of agile human resources using a soft capabilities approach to digital transformation in the Islamic Republic of Iran Railways. Methods and Materials: This developmental-applied, exploratory-descriptive study employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, 15 experts, senior managers, human resource and information technology specialists, railway industry managers, and university faculty members were selected through purposive and snowball sampling until theoretical saturation was reached. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using MAXQDA 2020 through open, axial, and selective coding. Coding reliability was assessed using Holsti’s agreement coefficient. In the quantitative phase, the same 15 experts completed pairwise comparison checklists for Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM), and the structural analyses were performed in MATLAB. In addition, 191 railway human resource employees were selected through stratified random sampling and completed a 40-item researcher-developed questionnaire. Findings: Qualitative analysis identified seven major dimensions: digital transformation leadership and governance, human resource agility, organizational culture, information technology infrastructure, customer satisfaction and processes, financial and operational performance, and continuous learning and growth. Digital transformational leadership emerged as the core category. Holsti’s agreement coefficient was 0.857. ISM analysis revealed a five-level hierarchical structure. Digital transformation leadership and governance occupied Level V with the highest driving power of 7 and dependence of 1, indicating its fundamental role. Organizational culture was positioned at Level IV. Human resource agility, information technology infrastructure, and continuous learning and growth were placed at Level III. Customer satisfaction and processes occupied Level II, while financial and operational performance represented the final outcome at Level I. MICMAC analysis classified leadership and organizational culture as independent driving variables, the three Level III dimensions as linkage variables, and customer/process and financial/operational outcomes as dependent variables. Conclusion: The findings indicate that agile human resources in digital transformation are primarily rooted in transformational digital leadership and organizational culture, which activate human, technological, and learning capabilities and ultimately improve organizational processes and financial and operational performance.

title: CRIMINAL LIABILITY FOR FINTECH-ENABLED ECONOMIC CRIMES: A COMPARATIVE LEGAL ANALYSIS
summary: Financial technology increases access to financial services but simultaneously introduces distinct risks, including money laundering, payment fraud, illegal digital lending, crypto-asset scams, data misuse, terrorist financing, and cyber-enabled theft. Although existing scholarship addresses these risks extensively, the literature remains fragmented by offense typologies, regulatory instruments, and national liability doctrines. This article examines the attribution of criminal liability to FinTech startups that commit, facilitate, or fail to prevent economic crime. The methodology involves a structured review of 30 English-language studies published primarily between 2020 and 2025, supplemented by comparative doctrinal analysis of legal and regulatory materials from the United States, the European Union, Indonesia, India, and China. The analysis identifies seven recurrent crime categories and three contrasting accountability models: broad vicarious corporate liability in the United States; harmonised regulation with nationally differentiated criminal liability rules in Europe; and heterogeneous Asian frameworks where formal corporate liability is often stronger than its practical enforcement. The principal finding reveals an implementation gap between the legal recognition of corporate responsibility and the evidential, institutional, and technological capacity necessary to enforce it. The article proposes an integrated liability model based on organisational fault, failure-to-prevent duties, proportionate compliance expectations, and technology-assisted supervision. This model aims to preserve innovation while ensuring that liability is responsive to startup governance, platform architecture, risk exposure, and compliance culture.

title: Inserting Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) Principles into Pension Fund Investments in Nigeria: Implications for Risk Management, Returns, And Sustainable Growth
summary: This study assessed the outcome of inserting Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) principles into pension fund investments in Nigeria, focusing on the interchange between risk management, financial performance and sustainable economic growth. Relying on panel data from Nigerian Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs), the study employed various analytical and data diagnostic methods including pooled Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Fixed Effects (FE), Random Effects (RE), and System Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimators. Also, the study used Sharpe ratio to gauge risk-adjusted performance and breaks down ESG integration into components into climate risk exposure, governance quality, infrastructure investment, and ESG screening mechanisms. The results show that integrating ESG principles has on general note significantly boost pension fund performance, mainly by enhancing risk-adjusted returns and lowering exposure to environmental and governance risks. Specifically, Climate risk exposure tends to limit performance, governance quality stands out as the most significant positive factor. Sustainable infrastructure investment also plays an enhancing role, albeit modestly, reflecting its long-term return potential. The study therefore recommends, amongst others that policymakers should focus on strengthening ESG regulatory frameworks, inject accurate disclosure standards, and as well encourage pension fund managers to invest in sustainable infrastructure projects.

title: Do All ESG Dimensions Matter Equally? Evidence from Taiwanese Financial Holding Companies
summary: This study examines the relationship between ESG performance and firm value using a sample of 13 Taiwanese financial holding companies over the period 2016–2025. Firm value is measured by Tobin's Q, while ESG performance is measured using the Taiwan ESG (TESG) rating. A series of pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression models is employed to examine the effects of overall ESG performance and its individual Environmental (E), Social (S), and Governance (G) dimensions. The results indicate that overall ESG performance is positively associated with firm value. Among the individual ESG dimensions, the Social dimension exhibits the most robust positive association with firm value and remains statistically significant after accounting for within-firm correlation. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating ESG as a multidimensional construct rather than relying solely on an aggregate ESG score. JEL classification numbers: G32. title: Determinants of FinTech Adoption: A Comparative Study of Millennials and Generation Z in Assam, India
summary: The rapid growth of Financial Technology (FinTech) has significantly transformed financial service delivery, particularly among younger generations. This study examines the determinants of FinTech adoption and compares adoption behaviour between Millennials and Generation Z using a quantitative approach. Primary data were collected through structured questionnaires from a sample of 390 respondents in Assam, India, and analysed using regression analysis and independent sample t-test. The results indicate that perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust, and price value have a significant positive influence on FinTech adoption, while perceived risk does not have a significant effect on adoption behaviour. The findings also reveal significant differences between Millennials and Generation Z, with Generation Z demonstrating higher preference for ease of use and convenience, whereas Millennials place greater emphasis on trust and risk considerations. The study highlights that FinTech adoption is influenced by a combination of technological and behavioural factors, with varying impact across generational cohorts. The findings provide valuable insights for FinTech service providers to design generation-specific strategies focusing on usability, trust-building, and risk reduction.

title: For an AI-focused Fintech the approach to trust and privacy must be decided at the business model level
summary: Purpose This research validates that professionals across six artificial intelligence (AI)-focused Fintech business models endorse the inclusion of trust-building and addressing privacy concerns at the business model level. Trust-building and reducing privacy concerns should be one of the building blocks of a modern business model. Design/methodology/approach This research applied a mixed-method approach, analysing 12 interviews with Fintech managers and a survey of 1,452 Fintech professionals in management or other senior technology positions such as systems architects. Findings The analysis verified that the trust-building methods and the methods to reduce privacy concerns should be decided at the business model level. Originality/value Trust-building and reducing privacy concerns are added to the nine existing building blocks of the popular Business Model Canvas. The updated Business Model Canvas with 10 building blocks captures more accurately the six AI-focused Fintech business modes identified.

title: Pengaruh Pengungkapan Corporate Social Responsibilityterhadap Kinerja Keuangan (Studi Pada Perusahaan Manufaktur yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia)
summary: Pengungkapan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) semakin menjadi bagian penting dalam pengelolaan perusahaan karena aktivitas manufaktur tidak hanya berorientasi pada pencapaian laba, tetapi juga memiliki konsekuensi terhadap lingkungan dan masyarakat. Pada perusahaan manufaktur subsektor kimia, kebutuhan pengungkapan CSR menjadi semakin relevan karena karakteristik operasionalnya memiliki risiko lingkungan dan sosial yang relatif tinggi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan menganalisis pengaruh pengungkapan Corporate Social Responsibility terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan manufaktur subsektor kimia yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2022–2024. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan tahunan dan laporan keberlanjutan perusahaan. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas 30 perusahaan yang dipilih dengan teknik purposive sampling, sehingga diperoleh 90 observasi. Pengungkapan CSR diukur menggunakan Corporate Social Responsibility Disclosure Index berdasarkan GRI Standards 2021, sedangkan kinerja keuangan diukur menggunakan Return on Assets (ROA). Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan regresi data panel dengan bantuan EViews 12 dan menghasilkan Random Effect Model sebagai model estimasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengungkapan CSR berpengaruh signifikan dengan arah negatif terhadap ROA, dengan nilai t-statistic sebesar -2,172920 dan probabilitas 0,0320. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan pengungkapan CSR dalam jangka pendek dapat meningkatkan beban dan biaya perusahaan sehingga menekan laba relatif terhadap total aset. Penelitian ini mengimplikasikan bahwa perusahaan perlu menempatkan CSR sebagai investasi strategis jangka panjang dan memastikan pengelolaan biaya CSR tetap efisien agar manfaat sosial, lingkungan, reputasi, dan ekonomi dapat tercapai secara berkelanjutan.

title: Sustainability as a Defensive Strategy: ESG, Risk Exposure, and Returns in US Stocks
summary: ABSTRACT We analyzed the relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) metrics, financial risk, and expected returns in the US stock market, using data from S&P 500 companies over the period from 2007 to 2022 using aggregate ESG scores from Refinitiv (LSEG). We employed an empirical approach that combines portfolio analysis based on ESG and ESG‐Momentum quintiles, traditional and tail risk measures (standard deviation, Value at Risk, and Expected Shortfall), higher order moments of return distributions (skewness and kurtosis), as well as cross‐sectional regressions using the method of Fama and MacBeth. We show that ESG scores, in isolation, do not exhibit significant predictive power over future returns. However, firms with high ESG performance are consistently associated with lower risk exposure, reflecting a more conservative and resilient profile. The ESG‐Momentum factor, although it does not consistently deliver superior returns, has shown greater stability and lower sensitivity to extreme losses. The findings suggest that ESG metrics add value primarily by mitigating financial risk rather than enhancing return potential. Thus, ESG functions as a strategic risk management mechanism that reduces firms' exposure to downside and tail risks. These results offer practical implications for investors and portfolio managers seeking defensive strategies with a sustainability focus.

title: The Limits of ESG Disclosure: Nonlinear Effects and Diminishing Returns in Corporate Sustainability
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid expansion of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure has transformed how firms communicate sustainability commitments, yet whether progressively greater disclosure remains equally associated with stronger environmental outcomes is unclear. This study examines whether the association between ESG disclosure and environmental performance is linear or characterized by diminishing marginal returns. Using a global panel of 1320 publicly listed firms and 12,480 firm‐year observations from 2010 to 2023, the analysis employs fixed effects, correlated random effects (CRE/Mundlak), quadratic, threshold, and spline models. The results reveal a concave association: ESG disclosure is associated with environmental performance at low and moderate disclosure levels, but the marginal association weakens as disclosure expands. The quadratic turning point and independently estimated threshold are both located around 61 points on the 0–100 disclosure scale, identifying a common region in which the positive disclosure association weakens substantially, although the alternative nonlinear specifications differ in their characterization of the relationship beyond that region. The weakening occurs earlier under weaker institutional and internal governance conditions, although subgroup differences are interpreted cautiously and supported by formal cross‐group tests. The findings are robust to alternative environmental outcomes, richer fixed‐effects structures, lagged specifications, alternative outlier treatments, and sectoral exclusions. Overall, the evidence supports diminishing marginal association, with threshold and spline estimates indicating broad saturation while the quadratic specification permits reversal only at very high disclosure levels. The study challenges the constant marginal‐effect assumption and highlights the importance of disclosure quality, materiality, credibility, and verification as reporting becomes more extensive.

title: Exploring the green HRM as a catalyst for sustainable business model: an integrated study of bibliometric and systematic literature review
summary: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has evolved from environmental compliance to become a strategic tool supporting sustainability-oriented business models. The study investigates the intellectual progression of GHRM and its connection to emerging sustainable business model frameworks through an integrated approach, combining bibliometric analysis, systematic literature review (SLR), and theoretical synthesis based on the TCCM framework. The bibliometric analysis encompassed 237 Scopus-indexed studies (2014– 2025), revealing growing research activity, key journals and authors, and emerging themes including Green Culture, Innovation, Circular Economy, and Digital Transformation. A subset of 24 studies, selected for quality and relevance, underwent detailed SLR synthesis, identifying seven Sustainable Business Model pathways: technology-driven, circular and regenerative, capability-based, governance and strategic alignment, behavioural and human-centric, Triple Bottom Line, and sector-specific models. The integrated findings explored that GHRM contributes to sustainability through mechanisms involving employee capabilities, organizational culture, green innovation, leadership, stakeholder alignment and technological capabilities. However, these relationships are not uniform across contexts, with organizational resources, technological readiness and sectoral conditions shaping outcomes. This study contributes by linking the intellectual development of GHRM to its various sustainable business model configurations and by integrating diverse theoretical perspectives to elucidate these interrelationships.

title: The Effects of IT Investment and ESG Integration on Firm Value: Evidence from an Emerging Economy
summary: This study examines whether IT investment intensity and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance jointly affect firm value in a frontier-market setting. The analysis uses an unbalanced panel of 201 non-financial firms listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange, comprising 875 firm-year observations from 2020 to 2024. Two-way firm and year fixed-effects models are estimated alongside pooled ordinary least squares specifications on identical data to distinguish within-firm dynamics from between-firm differences. In the pooled analysis, ESG performance is positively associated with firm value, with a one-standard-deviation increase corresponding to approximately 12.4 per cent of mean Tobin’s Q. The interaction between IT investment intensity and ESG performance is also positive, increasing the implied ESG valuation premium by about 58 per cent for firms one standard deviation above mean IT intensity. Pillar-level results indicate that this complementarity is concentrated in the environmental and governance dimensions rather than the social dimension. The pooled interaction is more evident among large, mature, and low-leverage firms. Under firm fixed effects, the main IT, ESG, and interaction coefficients become statistically insignificant, except for a positive, marginally significant interaction in technology-intensive sectors. Robustness, endogeneity, placebo, and attrition checks support the distinction between pooled and within-firm results. Overall, the evidence indicates that IT–ESG complementarity is primarily a persistent between-firm valuation pattern rather than a short-run within-firm pricing effect.

title: Peran Moderasi ESG pada Kinerja Perusahaan dalam Mempengaruhi Nilai Perusahaan Major Commercial Banks ASEAN-6
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji peran moderasi kualitas pengungkapan ESG pada pengaruh kecukupan modal, risiko kredit, dan likuiditas terhadap nilai perusahaan pada major commercial banks di ASEAN-6 periode 2020 hingga 2024. Sampel penelitian ini dipilih menggunakan purposive sampling, menghasilkan 30 bank dengan 142 observasi yang dianalisis menggunakan FEM dan MRA dengan pendekatan kluster bank. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan CAR dan NPL tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap nilai perusahaan. Sedangkan LDR berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan menunjukkan bahwa tingginya rasio likuiditas akan meningkatkan risiko pendanaan yang dinilai investor dapat mengganggu stabilitas operasional serta mengikis kepercayaan publik, sehingga menurunkan nilai perusahaan. Temuan utama menunjukkan moderasi kualitas pengungkapan ESG terbukti memperkuat pengaruh positif CAR terhadap nilai perusahaan serta mengonfirmasikan adanya anomali teoritis yang menarik. Namun, moderasi kualitas pengungkapan ESG pada pengaruh NPL maupun LDR tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap nilai perusahaan. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa peran moderasi kualitas pengungkapan ESG pada dampak kinerja keuangan perbankan dan nilai perusahaan bersifat selektif dan kontekstual. Serta berdasarkan hasil dan temuan diharapkan dapat memberikan rekomendasi strategis bagi manajemen bank, investor, dan regulator dalam harmonisasi standar pelaporan ESG di kawasan ASEAN-6.

title: How External Regulations Influence ESG Integration in Construction Firms: A Managerial Cognition Perspective
summary: Abstract Limited understanding of how external regulations influence construction firms’ environmental, social, and governance (ESG) integration constrains policy effectiveness and industry sustainability performance. Drawing on neo-institutional theory and managerial cognition (MC), we examine how regulations influence construction firms’ ESG integration by leveraging managerial cognition of the ESG-firm performance link. Data from Chinese A-share listed construction firms is analyzed through ordinary least squares (OLS) regression and qualitative comparative analysis. Results show that government procurement projects, subsidies, and the ESG Best Practice Case Collection directly foster ESG integration, while ESG disclosure regulations and government penalties exert little impact. Peer ESG rating gaps also discourage ESG integration. Five regulatory configurations are identified, with normative pressures strengthening coercive effects. Managerial cognition mediates the influence of penalties, procurement projects, and best-practice collection on ESG integration. The findings highlight that project-based operational models influence the relationship between external regulations and ESG integration in construction firms. By revealing institutional and cognitive pathways, this study advances neo-institutional theory and ESG literature and offers actionable insights for policy makers and firms to integrate ESG.

summary: Introduction. The growing importance of non-financial value drivers, increasing demands for business transparency, and the spread of the sustainable development concept are making the use of integrated reporting as a strategic enterprise management tool increasingly relevant. Traditional financial reporting, oriented mainly toward reflecting past business events, does not fully satisfy management's needs for comprehensive information about the business model, risks, and value-creation prospects. Purpose. The purpose of the article is to investigate the theoretical and methodological foundations of using integrated reporting as a strategic management tool and to substantiate a mechanism for integrating key performance indicators (KPIs) into the management accounting and reporting system. Methods. The study employs methods of analysis, synthesis, comparison, generalization and systematization of scientific sources, as well as modelling to construct a conceptual framework. Results. The key advantages of integrated reporting for strategic goal setting, risk management, and long-term value creation are identified. Integrated reporting performs not only an informational but also a strategic function, contributing to higher-quality managerial decisions, greater business transparency, and the implementation of a sustainable development strategy. title: Green entrepreneurial leadership as a catalyst for environmental performance in hospitality SMEs: the role of green commitment and innovation
summary: Purpose This study investigates the role of green entrepreneurial leadership in relation to environmental performance within tourism and hospitality SMEs, with a specific focus on the mediating mechanisms of green commitment and green innovation. Grounded in stakeholder theory and the resource-based view (RBV), the research seeks to explain how leadership-driven behaviors are associated with ecological outcomes in a sector highly exposed to environmental pressures and stakeholder scrutiny. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a structured questionnaire distributed to managerial and professional employees working in SMEs in the hospitality industry in Greater Cairo, Egypt. Using PLS-SEM, the study rigorously tested measurement and structural models to examine the hypothesized relationships and mediating effects. Findings The results indicate that green entrepreneurial leadership affects positively environmental performance, green commitment, and green innovation. Furthermore, both green commitment and green innovation were found to be positively affected environmental performance. Most importantly, the analysis revealed that green commitment and green innovation mediate the relationship between green entrepreneurial leadership and environmental performance. Social implications The findings suggest that promoting green entrepreneurial leadership in hospitality SMEs can foster environmentally responsible organizational practices by strengthening employees' green commitment and facilitating green innovation. These outcomes may contribute to improved environmental sustainability within the tourism sector and support broader sustainable development objectives. Originality/value This study advances Stakeholder Theory by showing that SMEs can proactively respond to stakeholder pressures through ecological value creation. It extends the growing literature on green entrepreneurial leadership within tourism and hospitality SMEs and demonstrates the dual mediating roles of green commitment and green innovation. Additionally, the study contributes to the RBV by conceptualizing leadership, commitment, and innovation as strategic internal capabilities associated with stronger environmental performance and the effective response to external stakeholder expectations.

title: Practice Briefing: The significance of real estate in sovereign wealth funds
summary: Purpose Sovereign wealth funds (SWFs) are amongst the leading institutional investors globally, with over $16.9tn in assets. This practice briefing examines the significance of real estate in SWF portfolios. Case studies of leading SWFs are presented concerning their real estate portfolios. The strategic implications for SWFs and real estate professionals are also assessed. Design/methodology/approach A range of information sources are used to assess the significance of real estate in SWF portfolios. Case studies highlight the strategies used by SWFs to obtain their real estate exposure. Findings SWFs are amongst the leading global real estate investors, having over $465bn in real estate assets. They use a range of effective strategies to obtain their real estate exposure, including direct real estate, joint ventures/co-investment, non-listed real estate funds and debt financing. Direct real estate and joint ventures/co-investment are seen as the preferred real estate strategies by SWFs. Practical implications Real estate is an important asset class for SWFs, typically accounting for 7% of their total portfolio. In-house teams and external real estate asset managers are used to deliver their real estate agenda. Opportunities for leading real estate professionals are available to assist SWFs deliver their real estate agenda going forward. Originality/value This is the first paper to examine the significance of real estate in SWF portfolios at a global level. Major insights are provided concerning how SWFs obtain their real estate exposure and how they deliver their real estate strategy. This study expands our understanding of the significance of real estate as an important asset class by leading institutional investors.

title: Pengaruh Struktur Modal, Likuiditas, dan Profitabilitas terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada Perusahaan Non-Perbankan LQ45
summary: Firm value served as a primary reflection of overall corporate performance and market perception, which was heavily influenced by underlying financial decisions. In modern capital markets, maintaining an optimal balance between financing risks and asset efficiency remained a critical challenge for large-scale enterprises listed on benchmark indices like the LQ45. This study aimed to examine the empirical effect of capital structure, liquidity, and profitability on firm value among non-banking companies consistently listed on the LQ45 Index during the 2020–2024 period. Employing a quantitative associative approach with purposive sampling, a final dataset of 17 companies yielding 85 balanced panel observations was analyzed using panel data regression, preceded by model selection procedures through the Chow and Hausman tests which established the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) as the optimal specification. The empirical results demonstrated that while capital structure (DER) and liquidity (CR) exhibited a negative yet statistically insignificant effect, profitability (ROE) showed a positive but statistically insignificant effect on firm value (PBV). Nevertheless, all independent variables simultaneously exerted a significant joint influence on firm value. These findings aligned with the Efficient Market Theory (semi-strong form), indicating that public fundamental indicators had been priced-in by market participants. This research contributed valuable insights to corporate finance literature by highlighting that financial ratios were evaluated holistically by investors rather than in isolation, suggesting that corporate management needed to focus on comprehensive long-term value creation strategies, while future studies were encouraged to incorporate broader external or macroeconomic indicators.

title: The Yunus Centre as a Global Hub for Social Business: Operationalising Ethical Stakeholder Engagement and Creating Sustainable Value
summary: This study examines how the Yunus Centre (YC) ecosystem operationalises social business principles through stakeholder-centred hybrid governance. Drawing on institutional logics and hybridity perspectives, the study integrates Corporate Social Responsibility, Social Enterprise, Social Entrepreneurship Theory, Stakeholder Theory, the Social Business Model, and the Triple Bottom Line. A qualitative multi-case study analyses four interconnected cases across Taiwan, Germany, and Bangladesh, based on 40 semi-structured interviews, institutional documents, and field observations. Findings show that the YC ecosystem functions as an interconnected hybrid governance system in which complementary governance logics enable shared purpose, contextual adaptability, stakeholder coordination, and sustainable multidimensional value creation.

Detailed Description ### 4.1 Overview This systematic review examines the critical role of community participation, institutional coordination, and individual responsibility in environmental protection, with a particular focus on rural India. Authored by Geruganti Sudhakar, Faculty at RGUKT (Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies), IIIT Basar, the paper synthesizes contemporary scholarship from environmental governance, community-based natural resource management (CBNRM), behavioral science, and public policy to construct a comprehensive framework for understanding environmental protection as a collective responsibility. The central premise of this review is that environmental protection cannot be achieved through government regulation alone; it requires the active engagement of individuals, communities, civil society organizations, and institutions working in coordinated partnership. Drawing on the Telugu news article “పర్యావరణ పరిరక్షణ ప్రతి ఒక్కరి బాధ్యత” (Environmental Protection is Everyone’s Responsibility), published in V6 Velugu, the paper argues that top-down approaches, while necessary, are insufficient without grassroots participation, local ownership, and behavioral change. ### 4.2 The Problem: Environmental Degradation and Governance Gaps The paper begins by establishing the magnitude of India’s environmental challenges. India ranked 176th out of 180 countries in the 2024 Environmental Performance Index (EPI), highlighting significant gaps in environmental policy implementation. The country loses approximately 1.5 million hectares of forest cover annually, and air pollution alone causes an estimated 1.67 million premature deaths each year. These figures underscore the urgent need for innovative governance approaches that mobilize all segments of society. The V6 Velugu article reports on a Vanamahotsavam (forest festival) program organized in Cherial, Telangana, where the Forest Department, local administration, and community members collaboratively planted saplings and distributed them to households. The event brought together officials including the Forest Divisional Officer (FDO), local MLA, and community leaders. The article emphasizes that environmental protection is not solely the responsibility of the government but a collective duty of every individual. This event represents a microcosm of broader environmental governance challenges and opportunities. Tree plantation drives are among the most visible and popular environmental interventions in India, yet their long-term effectiveness depends on factors that extend far beyond the initial planting event: post-plantation care, community ownership, institutional support, and behavioral change. The article’s emphasis on distributing saplings to households is particularly significant, as it transfers responsibility for tree care from the state to individual citizens—a strategy that can enhance survival rates and foster environmental stewardship. ### 4.3 Environmental Protection as a Cross-Cutting Issue The review emphasizes that environmental protection is inherently cross-cutting, intersecting with public health, economic development, social equity, and climate resilience. Women, who often bear primary responsibility for fuelwood collection, water fetching, and agricultural work, are disproportionately affected by environmental degradation. The review also highlights the health dimensions of environmental protection. Air pollution, water contamination, and exposure to toxic substances are major contributors to morbidity and mortality in India. By protecting the environment, communities also protect their own health and well-being—a point that underscores the interconnectedness of environmental and public health agendas. ### 4.4 Community Participation and Environmental Outcomes: The Evidence A substantial portion of the review is devoted to examining the empirical evidence linking community participation to environmental outcomes. The findings are organized around several themes: **Community-Based Natural Resource Management (CBNRM)** CBNRM emerged in the 1980s and 1990s as a paradigm that recognizes local communities as stewards of natural resources rather than passive beneficiaries or obstacles to conservation. title: Beyond Delegation Depth: Audit Reach, Enforcement Reach, and Management Coverage in Recursive AI Delegation
summary: Recursive AI delegation is commonly constrained by hop counts, but equally deep structures can differ in whether authority remains attributable, auditable and stoppable. This paper separates path-level management-substrate coverage from contiguous audit reach, structural enforcement reach and timely enforcement reach, all relative to an explicit assurance context. Non-monotone reach is reported as a set, and graph-level denial is evaluated against the effective authorization support and revocation objective. A timed support-closure identity connects authorization topology to the deadline of effective denial. Strict effect-boundary enforcement is distinguished from residual exposure bounded jointly by expiry and aggregate execution controls. An indistinguishability argument shows why sample evidence alone cannot guarantee an unsampled branch property, for either audit or enforcement; the operational distinction is between population evidence and universal prevention. Further elementary results identify a depth-only decision limitation and conditions under which actual propagation delay increases revocation-race risk. Worked calculations are logical witnesses, not empirical results. The resulting admissibility framework incorporates impact, reversibility, coverage, reach, support topology, timing and evidence freshness. A prospective evaluation contract separates pre-action certificates from held-out outcomes, includes component ablations, request and follow-up accounting, competing hypotheses and full assurance costs, and prevents absence of a guarantee from being counted as execution failure. The contribution is this operational composition, not the underlying delegation, revocation, sampling or complete-mediation mechanisms. Note on Version 2.0: this version revises the registered v1.0 (about 12,100 to 16,000 words). It adds a timed support-closure result and temporal composition of closure, worked logical cases and a conditional timing result, certificate evaluation with bounded exposure, and a rebuilt Section 9 covering the measurement contract and minimal test design, external measurements and transfer conditions, discriminating predictions with competing explanations, and a joint test of support, timing and current evidence. No empirical result is claimed: the supporting archive records 53 exact analytical checks on cited summaries, external evidence records, a public result recalculation, a novelty audit, a change log and a validation record with SHA-256 checksums. Files: the v2.0 manuscript and that supporting archive. This paper derives from the author's broader Information Ecosystem Theory, which remains unpublished at the time of this release; it is written to stand alone.

title: Machine Learning et audit interne intelligent : une approche orientée décision pour la détection des anomalies financières et la réduction du risque de fraude chez les entreprises marocaines
summary: Résumé La transformation digitale des organisations a profondément modifié l’environnement informationnel de l’audit interne. L’augmentation du volume, de la granularité et de l’interconnexion des données financières met sous tension les approches traditionnelles fondées sur l’échantillonnage et les contrôles a posteriori. Dans ce contexte, cette étude analyse la contribution du machine learning au développement d’un audit interne orienté vers l’analyse et la décision au sein des entreprises marocaines. La recherche repose sur un dispositif quantitatif en deux phases. Une première étape identifie les entreprises disposant d’un ERP opérationnel et d’outils de machine learning. Une seconde étape teste un modèle de médiation séquentielle par PLS-SEM auprès de 32 entreprises technologiquement équipées. Les résultats montrent que le machine learning n’agit pas directement sur la création de valeur. Son effet est indirect : l’amélioration de la détection des anomalies renforce la qualité du jugement des auditeurs, ce qui réduit le risque de fraude et accroît la valeur ajoutée perçue. Le modèle explique 31 % de la variance de cette création de valeur. En articulant technologie, décision et gouvernance, l’étude éclaire les mécanismes par lesquels l’analytique avancée soutient la gestion du risque dans un contexte émergent. Abstract The digital transformation of organizations has profoundly reshaped the informational environment of internal auditing. The growing volume, granularity, and interconnectedness of financial data challenge traditional audit approaches based on sampling and ex post controls. In this context, this study examines the contribution of machine learning to the development of a decision-oriented and analytically driven internal audit function within Moroccan organizations. The research follows a two-phase quantitative design. The first phase identifies companies equipped with operational ERP systems and machine learning tools. title: Kuwait Voluntary National Review 2023
summary: The State of Kuwait’s 2023 Voluntary National Review (VNR) is its second assessment of progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) since 2019. Guided by the “New Kuwait 2035” vision, all 17 SDGs have been integrated into national planning, aligning each pillar with specific SDG clusters. The review highlights achievements in education, healthcare, food security, social protection, gender equality, and climate action, including carbon neutrality targets for 2050–2060. Strong institutions, such as the National Sustainable Development Committee (NSDC), the National Observatory for Sustainable Development (NOSD), and the State Audit Bureau (SAB), ensure oversight, data-driven policy, and financial integrity. Despite COVID-19 disruptions, Kuwait showed resilience through digital transformation, reskilling, and international support. Completed and ongoing projects span economic diversification, private sector growth, governance, infrastructure, environmental sustainability, health, and global engagement, with overall SDGs achievement projected to rise from 60.5 in 2021 to 61.3 by 2030.

title: Cybersecurity Legal Framework in Saudi Arabia: A Comparative Analysis
summary: Background: In today's digital era, especially in a Vision 2030 country like the KSA, cybersecurity has turned into an integral legal and institutional duty, with increasing reliance on digital infrastructure, personal data, and electronic transactions. Objective: In this study, the researchers aim to assess the efficiency of Saudi Arabia's legal and regulatory frameworks for cybersecurity in the protection of national infrastructures, personal rights, and the digital economy, as well as in facing new cyber risks. Method: The research is of an analytical nature that discusses the main Saudi legislations such as the Anti-Cyber Crime Law, Personal Data Protection Law, Electronic Transactions Law, Telecommunications and Information Technology Law, and the Essential Cybersecurity Controls issued by the National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA). A comparative approach is used, utilizing international standards such as ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27032, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and some European regulatory models. Findings: The Saudi framework encompasses criminal protection, governance, risk management, compliance, and personal data protection, which enhances national security and trust in the digital environment. The roles and responsibilities are no longer limited to technical teams, but include Boards of Directors, Executive Management, and compliance teams. Due diligence and regulatory compliance are becoming a significant factor in determining liability. New technologies like artificial intelligence, cloud computing, IoT, and cross-border threats are new challenges that need constant adjustment in legislation and institutions. Conclusion: Saudi Arabia's cybersecurity framework exhibits significant alignment with international standards and best practices. It has to be constantly updated and reinforced through regulation, tighter institutional compliance, and development of a legal and cybersecurity culture that favours a digital transformation and sustainable development.

title: THE QUANTUM MOMENTONIC ENERGY THEOREM The Missing Variable in Quantum Energy Accounting
summary: The kinetic energy of every quantum system decomposes exactly into two terms: T_flow, the energy of net momentum flow, and T_org, the energy of momentum organization — the Quantum Momentonic Potential. This decomposition follows from the Madelung representation ψ = √ρ · exp(iS/ℏ), established in 1927. It is an exact identity, not an approximation. What is new is the recognition that T_org is the quantum analogue of the Momentonic Potential Energy developed in classical Momentodynamics, and that its separate tracking provides a unified accounting framework for six major quantum phenomena: zero-point energy, the Casimir effect, spontaneous emission, quantum tunneling, the Lamb shift, and the Aharonov-Bohm effect. Each involves a change in T_org that, when tracked explicitly, unifies their energetic interpretation. The paper demonstrates this through three canonical systems. In the quantum harmonic oscillator, the zero-point energy ½ℏω is shown to consist of ¼ℏω of pure T_org — the minimum Quantum Momentonic Potential, which is the Dynamic Ground State of the mode. In the particle in a box, 100% of the energy is T_org; the particle has energy because its probability distribution is organized, not because it moves. In the hydrogen atom, the 1s electron has 13.6 eV of kinetic energy with zero momentum flow; falling deeper into the Coulomb well increases T_org, not decreases it. The Quantum Momentonic Energy Theorem is stated: E_total = T_flow + T_org + ⟨V⟩. Each term must be tracked independently. The conservation law was never in question — the standard resolutions are correct. What was incomplete was the explicit identification of the common accounting variable. The Quantum Momentonic Potential provides that variable. Madelung discovered the decomposition. Bohm discovered the potential. Momentonics discovers the accounting. title: Provincial Pollution-Control Investment and Wind–Huazheng Environmental Peer-Position Distance
summary: ESG-rating disagreement is commonly attributed to persistent differences across providers. We examine variation within a fixed pair by relating province-year pollution-control investment intensity to contemporaneous Wind and Huazheng environmental scores for 4,797 Chinese A-share firms during 2018–2023. We standardize each provider’s scores within its industry-year distribution and express them on a common peer scale. The primary outcome is the absolute gap between the two resulting peer positions, which shows how far apart the Wind and Huazheng scores place the same firm within its industry-year peer group. The signed Wind-minus-Huazheng difference preserves provider orientation. A one-standard-deviation increase in investment intensity is associated with 0.019 additional distance units, or 2.800 percent of the outcome standard deviation, with a restricted Webb-bootstrap p value of .005. The same increase is associated with a 0.046-unit decline in the signed difference, orienting the relationship toward a higher Huazheng-implied position. On the common pre-clipping scale, the Huazheng position accounts for most of the signed association. The Wind position changes little. The wider distance also appears within firms and under equal province-year weighting. Disagreement changes across places and years even when the provider pair remains fixed. In province-years with higher pollution-control investment intensity, the peer positions implied by Wind and Huazheng scores lie farther apart, which means that the choice between Wind and Huazheng matters more for comparisons and threshold decisions.

title: Mapping Maqāṣid al-Sharī‘ah Research in Indonesia’s Digital Business: Trends, Domains, and Future Research Agenda
summary: The rapid development of digital business in Indonesia has encouraged the growing use of maqāṣid al-syarī'ah in Islamic economics research, yet the development, methodological quality, and conceptual orientation of this literature remain insufficiently mapped. This study examines publication trends, digital-business domains, methodological characteristics, maqāṣid al-syarī'ah dimensions, and research gaps in nationally accredited SINTA journals published between 2022 and 2026. A structured literature review was conducted using systematic search, screening, critical appraisal, and descriptive content analysis procedures. Literature was identified through GARUDA and Google Scholar, while journal accreditation was verified through the official SINTA portal. Seven studies satisfied the eligibility criteria and were included in the final synthesis. The literature is concentrated in digital marketing and Sharia fintech/e-wallets, each represented by two studies, while e-commerce, digital economic empowerment, and the digital economy are represented by one study each. Methodological appraisal indicates heterogeneous evidentiary strength and uneven reporting quality across empirical and library-based studies. In terms of maqāṣid dimensions, ḥifẓ al-māl appears in all seven studies (100.0%), while ḥifẓ al-dīn, ḥifẓ al-nafs, ḥifẓ al-'aql, and ḥifẓ al-nasl each appear in five studies (71.4%). Contrary to the initial coding, ḥifẓ al-bi'ah is explicitly incorporated in one study (14.3%), whereas ḥifẓ al-ummah is not explicitly operationalized. The principal research gap is therefore not the complete absence of contemporary maqāṣid, but their limited and uneven integration across digital-business research.

title: An Autonomous Evaluation Framework for Quantitative Robustness, Faithful Explainability, and Failure-Mode Auditing in Vision Models
summary: Object detectors in production are certified on a single number—in-distribution mAP—which says nothing about adversarial vulnerability, sensitivity to sensor corruptions, the faithfulness of their explanations, or the failure modes that dominate in the field. We present an autonomous evaluation framework that quantifies all four dimensions in a single post-training pass and turns them into objective, thresholded risk flags that gate deployment. The framework composes six states: (1) multi-attack adversarial testing using FGSM, PGD-20, and Carlini-Wagner L2 attacks; (2) corruption robustness across five severity levels; (3) MC Dropout uncertainty decomposition into epistemic and aleatoric variance paired with Expected Calibration Error monitoring; (4) quantitative XAI fidelity via Deletion and Insertion AUC with Grad-CAM++ and Eigen-CAM; (5) hard-negative mining audit clustering 450 field failures; and (6) an LLM reporting state with a deterministic fallback guaranteeing sub-millisecond execution. Across all six states, every analytic result is a deterministic function of weights and inputs, providing bit-for-bit audit reproducibility.
